To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the diet with the highest content of nutrients and energy did not necessarily result in the highest performance of A. ludens.

(1) the diet with the highest nutritional content did not result in the best performance in terms of larval survival, adult emergence, and flight capacity, (2) diets with lower nutritional content resulted in a higher percent of pupae that eclosed as adults, and (3) the diets with lower nutritional value are less expensive to produce.
a high content and multiple sources of proteins in the artificial diet do not necessarily translate into better performance of artificially re-ared fruit flies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the efficiency of mass-rearing the Mediterranean fruit fly, Ceratitis capitata (Wiedemann), for the sterile insect technique (SIT).
the development of a low-cost artificial diet that is nutritionally adequate for rearing A. ludens for a sterile insect program.
the optimization of artificial rearing diets for A. lndens and the effects of these diets on the quality and performance of the reared flies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the diet that is most cost efficient and provides the best overall performance is the one that provides the best balance of the nutrients and energy required by the insect, in the correct proportions, and that is the diet that provides the most efficient use of the resources.
there was no significant difference in the quality of the flies rearing on any of the diets.
the diet with the highest nutritional value was not necessarily the most cost effective diet for rearing A. ludens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most important nutrients for the performance of artificially-reared A. ludens are the protein, lipids, carbohydrates, and energy content of the diet.
the best performing diet for A. luden s was the one that was the least expensive to produce.
a diet that is not nutritionally complete may be adequate to support development and reproduction of the Mexican fruit fly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a high nutrient and energy content in a diet is not a prerequisite for high-quality fruit flies.
a high protein diet is not necessary to obtain high performance in A. ludens.
it is important to consider both the cost and the performance when designing diets for artificial mass rearing.
